title: Epochal KV Rotation & Spillback Scheduler for Asymmetric GPU Residency
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement an epochal rotation and spillback scheduling mechanism to reduce OOMs and tail latency under asymmetric GPU residency. The goal is to make a paged/blocked KV cache more robust when multiple workstreams with mismatched token affinities compete for limited GPU memory, without sacrificing continuous batching throughput.
context: We continue to see tail latency spikes and transient OOMs when long-running chat sessions (large KV residency) are mixed with high-throughput short requests. Existing slab/paged allocators reclaim based on LRU-like heuristics which do not account for token affinity, batch alignment or current batching depth. This ticket proposes an epoch-based rotation plus spillback scheduler that prefers eviction candidates based on epoch age, token-affinity score, batch alignment cost, and a spillback policy to host memory when eviction would harm in-flight batched requests.
goals: Reduce GPU OOMs under mixed workloads by 60% in stress tests
Keep median and P95 token generation latency within 10% of baseline for steady-state batching workloads
Avoid synchronous stalls during eviction by using async spillback and prioritized rotations
Provide per-tenant (or per-request-group) residency budgets and graceful degradation paths
acceptance_criteria: Design doc reviewed and approved by infra and runtime leads
Implementation passes unit and integration tests (simulated oversubscription scenarios)
Benchmark: 60% fewer OOMs on mixed traces from customer-simulated workloads
Benchmark: P95 latency regression < 10% vs current runtime on dedicated GPU runs
Feature gated behind a runtime flag; can be enabled per-cluster in config
implementation_plan: Phase 1 - Design: finalize scoring function (epoch_age, token_affinity, batch_alignment_cost, last_access) and data structures (epoch buckets + resident sets)
Phase 2 - Prototype: integrate epoch buckets into existing paged KV allocator; add async spillback queue to host-staging layer
Phase 3 - Scheduler: implement spillback scheduler that considers in-flight batch window; prefer rotation vs immediate evict when batch_alignment_cost is high
Phase 4 - Instrumentation: add per-token and per-request metrics, residency traces, and tracing hooks to visualize rotations
Phase 5 - Canary: enable on dedicated test cluster with mixed synthetic + sampled production traces; iterate
Phase 6 - Rollout: gradual enable with runtime-flag and per-customer residency caps
design_decisions: Use epochs (coarse-grained time buckets) instead of strict LRU to avoid hot-item churn during continuous batching
Prefer spillback to host memory for large contiguous KV blocks if async spillback latency < configured threshold
Scoring function combines epoch_age and token_affinity with tunable weights to allow workload-specific policies
Avoid synchronous device->host copies on hot-path; always perform spillback asynchronously and allow in-flight batches to complete using cached GPU pins until safe
Expose a 'residency_budget' per-tenant that is throttleable via control plane; when exceeded, scheduler enters aggressive rotation mode
tradeoffs: Epochal rotation reduces noisy eviction churn but introduces coarser granularity—some stale entries might linger slightly longer
Async spillback reduces tail stalls but increases host memory usage and network traffic for remote hosts
Scoring complexity adds overhead to allocation path; mitigate with incremental scoring and sampling heuristics
Per-tenant budgets add management surface area; necessary for multi-tenant fairness

open_questions: What is the long-term host-memory cap we should enforce for spillback in Dedicated clusters? (ops input required)
How to surface per-tenant residency alerts in Console without spamming customers? (UX/PM input)
Should scoring weights be auto-tuned based on observed workload, or remain static and configurable? (research tradeoff)
If a large KV block is pinned by an in-flight batch, what's the max allowed grace period before we force preemption?
risk_mitigation: Feature gated behind runtime flag and can be disabled cluster-wide
Start with conservative weights and a high threshold for async spillback to avoid unnecessary host traffic
Run canaries on non-customer-facing dedicated pools and compare OOM/latency metrics before broader rollout
Implement circuit-breaker around spillback queue to fall back to immediate eviction if host memory pressure skyrockets
testing_plan: Unit tests for epoch bucket maintenance, scoring function edge cases
Integration tests that simulate continuous batching and mixed session affinities
Fuzz tests for scheduler under rapidly changing batch depths
Performance bench harness using customer-sampled traces (stored in s3://redwood-perf/kv-traces/2026/mixed)
Canary evaluation with A/B traffic split and dashboards comparing OOMs and P95 latency
notes: This approach intentionally favors stability during continuous batching workloads by avoiding tight LRU eviction. If successful, it will be a building block for higher-level routing policies (e.g., prefer cold-hosting for long-running sessions) and for the console to provide actionable residency controls to customers.
